subject: inconsistency between tiling and per base approach

messages.author: c46d30f877cfc51d
messages.subject: inconsistency between tiling and per base approach
parts:
Hello everyone,

I recently tried using Methylkit to extract both differentially methylated bases and regions. My preliminary results showed that using tiling function (mincov=5), I identified few DMRs with more than 20% difference. Here is one for example:

> normalize=normalizeCoverage(myobj)

> filtered.myobj=filterByCoverage(normalize,lo.count=5,lo.perc=NULL,

                                      hi.count=NULL,hi.perc=99.9)

> tiles=tileMethylCounts(filtered.myobj,win.size=530,step.size=530)

> meth=unite(tiles, destrand=TRUE) # destrand=TRUE shouldn't change anything here

> covariates=data.frame(env=c(rep("cap",20),rep("qui",19)))

> myDiff=calculateDiffMeth(meth,covariates=covariates, mc.cores=10)


And the output:

chr start end strand pvalue qvalue meth.diff

scf00205       1814001 1815000 *       6.11516534161915e-24    3.70110711076965e-22    -23.9084372045925



Yet, even if they are different analyses, I would expect to retrieve differentially methylated bases (mincov=5) within those regions. Here is my code:


> normalize=normalizeCoverage(myobj)

> filtered.myobj=filterByCoverage(normalize,lo.count=5,lo.perc=NULL,

   +                                   hi.count=NULL,hi.perc=99.9)

> meth=unite(filtered.myobj, destrand=TRUE)

> myDiff=calculateDiffMeth(meth,covariates=covariates,num.cores=5)


 And the output looks like:


chr start end strand pvalue qvalue meth.diff

scf00205 1806551 1806551 + 0.493963740899511 0.577385407864017 -0.35221668852341

scf00205 1821575 1821575 + 0.489396888209388 0.574724500221494 0.447879954588082


So basically very few differences within this specific region... How is this possible if tiling summarizes all the bases information within a specified region ?


Thank you,


Jérémy

messages.author: ab8277113f65c05e
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] inconsistency between tiling and per base approach
parts:
When you tile on methylRawList objects you are most likely including CpGs that are not covered on all samples and using them for summary. And in your base resolution comparison, you only use CpGs that are covered in all samples, the CpGs that are used in the the tile summary may not be there anymore. This is the caveat but also good thing about tiling, you can use information from CpGs that are not covered in all samples. 

if you want to use CpGs that are covered in all samples tile on methylBase object.

Best,
Altuna
